name: Bob
description: A researcher who links user needs, interaction designs, observations and findings to supported design decisions.

concepts.label: Alignment
concepts.definition: Agreement between a user's understanding of an AI assistant and its actual capabilities. This is not ontology-term correspondence.

concepts.label: User control
concepts.definition: The ways people can inspect, intervene in and direct system behavior; broader than reviewing semantic mappings.

concepts.label: Transparency
concepts.definition: How well a person can understand a system's behavior and its basis. Provenance may support transparency but is not equivalent to it.

concepts.label: User review decision
concepts.definition: A user's accept, modify or reject decision on a system-proposed item in an explicit review task. It is not an execution grant.

concepts.label: Presentation activity
concepts.definition: One individual research presentation inside a program session; not the whole session.

modules.name: Users, contexts, interaction designs and rationale

concepts.label: User need
concepts.definition: An evidenced need in a stated use context, distinct from a software feature or researcher's assumption.

concepts.label: Interaction context
concepts.definition: The people, activity and environment in which interaction takes place.

concepts.label: Interactive prototype
concepts.definition: A concrete version of an interactive design used for exploration or evaluation.

concepts.label: Interaction flow
concepts.definition: A sequence of user and system actions in a use context.

concepts.label: Design alternative
concepts.definition: A candidate interaction design, not an implemented or evaluated outcome.

concepts.label: Design rationale
concepts.definition: A documented reason for a design choice, linked to needs or research findings.

relations.definition: The research question or design responds to the stated need.
The need or flow is situated in this use context.
The prototype implements the interaction flow.
The candidate design has this documented rationale.

concepts.label: User study
concepts.definition: A study of interaction with a defined question, protocol and scope.

concepts.label: Study protocol
concepts.definition: A versioned plan describing procedure, tasks and measurements.

concepts.label: Study session
concepts.definition: One recorded execution of a study protocol; the fixture contains no real participants.

concepts.label: Task scenario
concepts.definition: A contextualized task used in a user study.

concepts.label: Observation
concepts.definition: A recorded observation from a specific study session, kept distinct from interpretation.

concepts.label: Participant consent record
concepts.definition: A record about a study participant's consent. It is not authorization for this agent to share data or execute operations.

relations.definition: The study or session follows the exact protocol version.
The protocol defines this study task.
The recorded session belongs to the study.
The study investigates this prototype version.
The observation was recorded in this study session.

modules.name: Findings, design implications and scholarly outputs

concepts.label: Research finding
concepts.definition: An interpretation supported by observations, with context and limitations.

concepts.label: Design implication
concepts.definition: A design suggestion derived from scoped research findings, not a universal rule.

concepts.label: Study report
concepts.definition: A report of study methods, observations, findings and limitations.

concepts.label: Prototype demonstration
concepts.definition: A demonstrator of a prototype, not evidence that the design was validated.

concepts.label: Design note
concepts.definition: A note linking interaction alternatives, reasons and evidence.

relations.definition: The finding is supported by the recorded observation.
The design implication follows from the scoped finding.
The implication informs this candidate interaction design.

fields.method: Separate proposed content, owner decisions and actual reception in the interface.
